title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: k is algebraically closed of characteristic different from 2. I is a 4-element set. The crossed-out line read 'card. ≥ ...'; the intended value is presumably 4, as the margin addition 'I de card. 4' suggests. J = J(I) is the 3-element set of partitions of I into two pairs. V = V(I) = V(J) is the Klein four-group of permutations of I that preserve every element of J. V acts simply transitively on I and acts trivially on J.

The previous pages construct a canonical 'model' X(I): a projective line carrying a faithful V(I)-action (V ⊂ PGL_2, possible since char ≠ 2). Each non-trivial involution has two fixed points. The quotient X(I)/V is a projective line Σ(J) with three branch points canonically indexed by J. Over a point ξ of Σ(J)^× (Σ(J) minus the three branch points), the fibre X(I)_ξ is a V-torsor.

Given a projective line X and an embedding I ↪ X of four distinct points, the three involutions of X attached to the three pair-partitions exist and commute. This gives a unique V ↪ PGL(X) inducing the regular action of V on I. The previous page then shows X ≅ X(I) ∧_V t for a V-torsor t, and X/V ≅ X(I)/V ≅ Σ(J) canonically.

The Theorem on this page packages this as an equivalence of groupoids:
{(X, I ↪ X) : X ≅ P^1, |I| = 4} ≃ {(I, ξ) : ξ ∈ Σ(J(I))^×}.
- Forward functor: ξ is the image of I in X/V ≅ Σ(J).
- Quasi-inverse: X = X(I) ∧_{V(I)} t(ξ, I), where t(ξ, I) = I ∧ X(I)_ξ^{-1} is the V-torsor of V-isomorphisms X(I)_ξ → I. The embedding I ↪ X is the fibre X_ξ ≅ X(I)_ξ ∧ t ≅ I.

When I has a base point i0, I is trivialised as a V-torsor. Then X ≅ X(I) as soon as a point of X(I) above ξ is chosen. More generally, 'admissible' (V-compatible) isomorphisms X ≅ X(I) correspond to V-isomorphisms I ≅ X(I)_ξ.

In modern terms this is a canonical, functorial-in-I identification of M_{0,4} with P^1 minus 3 points. Stack-theoretically, the stack of unordered 4-pointed lines is [Σ^×/S_4], with S_4 acting through S_4 → S_3 = Aut(J) and kernel V acting trivially. Hence the generic V-inertia, i.e. a V-gerbe over the λ-line modulo S_3. The page serves the 'Chirurgie des surfaces conformes' programme: it gives a canonical, choice-free description of the basic genus-0, 4-pointed building block, the M_{0,4} level of the Teichmüller tower.
errors: Notational inconsistency: V(J(I)) and V(I) are used interchangeably. This is harmless, since V(I) = V(J(I)) canonically, but it is written both ways in the same formula.
Σ(J)^× here versus Σ(J)^* on the previous page; both mean Σ(J) minus the three branch points.
The torsor convention I ∧ X(I)_ξ^{-1} (isomorphisms from the fibre to I) needs a consistent left/right V-action. This is left implicit ('expliciter' on the previous page).

The groupoid equivalence needs morphisms on the right-hand side to be bijections I → I' compatible with the induced maps Σ(J) → Σ(J'). This is not stated. With it, the automorphism groups match: V at generic ξ, enlarged at the special j-values.

ideas.what: Groupoid of 4 points on P^1 is canonically equivalent to the groupoid of pairs (I, ξ ∈ Σ(J(I))^×) via the Klein four-group quotient
ideas.modern_name: M_{0,4} ≅ P^1 − {0,1,∞} (λ-line), S_4 acting through S_3 with Klein kernel; stacky description [M_{0,4}/S_4]
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Legendre, Klein, cross-ratio theory); stack formulation folklore
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un Programme discusses M_{0,4} and the Teichmüller tower but not this explicit torsor formulation

ideas.what: Reconstruction of the 4-pointed line as a twist X(I) ∧_V t of a canonical V-equivariant model by the V-torsor t = I ∧ X(I)_ξ^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: twisting by torsors / descent; universal curve over M_{0,4} as Klein-cover of the λ-line

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, canonical, choice-free formulation of the classical identification of M_{0,4} with the λ-line via the Klein four-group. It is elegant and fits the surgery programme, but it is mathematically standard and contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Page number in the image is 91, not 88.
Margin addition after '(X, I↪X), où X est' reads 'I de card. 4' rather than 'I discret [?]'.
Crossed-out line: 'I un ens. de card. 4' (the digit is likely 4, not '≥').
'un foncteur [?] : on prend' is more plausibly 'un quasi-inverse : on prend'.
In the first displayed formula, the subscript is V(J(I)) with '= V(I)' written beneath it, as the transcription indicates.
